citation: pkgdown documentation.
specific_design_decision_supported: Reference index and article organization; local site build is a development product rather than CRAN source content.

citation: terra reference: compareGeom resample project crop mask.
specific_design_decision_supported: Geometry comparison precedes map algebra; explicit resampling or reprojection is required and continuous versus categorical methods differ.

citation: sf reference: st_crs and spatial geometry operations.
specific_design_decision_supported: CRS comparison uses the complete spatial reference; assigning a CRS does not transform coordinates; projected and geographic operations are distinguished.

citation: Wahba G. Spline Models for Observational Data. SIAM 1990.
specific_design_decision_supported: Thin-plate spline smoothing, penalized fitting, smoothing-parameter selection, and conditional interpretation of standard-error calculations.

citation: Nychka D et al. fields: Tools for Spatial Data.
specific_design_decision_supported: Use supported Tps predict and predictSE interfaces; retain fitted smoothing parameters and do not fabricate uncertainty without a fit.

citation: Pebesma EJ. Multivariable geostatistics in S: the gstat package. Computers & Geosciences 30:683-691.
specific_design_decision_supported: Use documented gstat objects for variograms, kriging, external drift, anisotropy, prediction variance, and conditional simulation.

citation: gstat krige and predict.gstat reference.
specific_design_decision_supported: Prediction variance is model conditional; nsim invokes sequential conditional simulation; record model, trend, neighborhood, random path, and seed.

citation: gstat variogram fit.variogram and vgm reference.
specific_design_decision_supported: Retain pair counts; validate cutoff and lag boundaries; document clockwise-from-North directional angles; preserve singular fits and weighting criterion.

citation: Roberts DR et al. Cross-validation strategies for data with temporal spatial hierarchical or phylogenetic structure. Ecography 40:913-929.
specific_design_decision_supported: Resampling must match the prediction task; spatial blocking evaluates transfer across separation and differs from random or leave-one-out validation.

citation: Wadoux AMJC et al. Spatial cross-validation is not the right way to evaluate map accuracy. Ecological Modelling 457:109692.
specific_design_decision_supported: Cross-validation performance under a resampling design is not automatically design-unbiased area-wide map accuracy; independent probability samples may use design weights.

citation: Schratz P et al. Hyperparameter tuning and performance assessment of statistical and machine-learning algorithms using spatial data. Ecological Modelling 406:109-120.
specific_design_decision_supported: Use spatially appropriate inner tuning partitions and a separate outer assessment when final performance is requested; prevent leakage.

citation: French JP. Confidence regions for the level curves of spatial data. Environmetrics 25:498-512.
specific_design_decision_supported: A formal simultaneous level-curve region needs a specific joint procedure; pointwise bands must not be labeled simultaneous confidence regions.

citation: Bolin D and Lindgren F. Excursion and contour uncertainty regions for latent Gaussian models. JRSS B 77:85-106.
specific_design_decision_supported: Joint excursion and contour regions depend on a latent Gaussian model and joint probabilities; marginal exceedance maps are different products.

citation: Bolin D and Lindgren F. Quantifying the Uncertainty of Contour Maps. JCGS 26:513-524.
specific_design_decision_supported: Contour-map quality and simultaneous contour uncertainty require spatial dependence; this release exposes empirical or Gaussian pointwise products with explicit terminology.

citation: Loaiciga HA et al. Review of Ground-Water Quality Monitoring Network Design. Journal of Hydraulic Engineering 118:11-37.
specific_design_decision_supported: Monitoring design begins with an explicit objective and constraints; statistical rankings do not replace hydrogeologic design or establish global optimality.

citation: Ohmer M Liesch T and Goldscheider N. On the Optimal Spatial Design for Groundwater Level Monitoring Networks. WRR 55:9454-9473.
specific_design_decision_supported: Distinguish predictive errors at held-out wells from descriptive difference to a reference surface; progressive coverage designs and model-dependent geostatistical designs answer different objectives.

citation: Heath RC. Basic Ground-Water Hydrology. USGS Water-Supply Paper 2220.
specific_design_decision_supported: Head is measured relative to a common datum; hydraulic gradient is head change per distance; modeled negative gradient indicates potential direction but is not velocity or a path.

citation: Taylor CJ and Alley WM. Ground-Water-Level Monitoring and the Importance of Long-Term Water-Level Data. USGS Circular 1217.
specific_design_decision_supported: Observation-well construction, screened interval, datum, timing, QA, network purpose, and long-term context are essential before comparing or mapping heads.

citation: USGS Circular 1217 Box A: Hydraulic Head and Factors Causing Changes in Ground Water Levels.
specific_design_decision_supported: A static water level represents head for the aquifer interval open to the well; confined potentiometric surface and unconfined water table terminology must remain distinct.

citation: USGS HA-748: Potential for vertical flow between aquifers.
specific_design_decision_supported: Paired heads at different depths indicate potential upward or downward movement; they do not by themselves provide vertical flux.

citation: USGS Groundwater Levels Service parameter definitions.
specific_design_decision_supported: Depth below land surface and water-level elevation relative to named vertical datums are distinct quantities and cannot be interchanged without reference metadata.

citation: Desbarats AJ et al. On the kriging of water table elevations using collateral information from a digital elevation model. Journal of Hydrology.
specific_design_decision_supported: A DEM can be a defensible secondary predictor for some water-table settings, but coverage and a supported relation are required and must be validated.

citation: Rivest M et al. Hydraulic head field estimation using kriging with an external drift: A way to consider conceptual model information. Journal of Hydrology 361:349-361.
specific_design_decision_supported: External drift can incorporate exhaustive auxiliary information; the predictor remains a statistical/model covariate and does not prove causality.

citation: Rocha MM Yamamoto JK and Fonteles HRN. Ordinary co-kriging versus kriging with external drift for a free-aquifer potentiometric level.
specific_design_decision_supported: External-drift behavior depends on correlation, spatial coverage, and network distribution; do not silently substitute a coordinate-only trend.

citation: USGS SIM 3509: Potentiometric-surface altitude in 2022 and groundwater-level changes in the Big Lost River Valley.
specific_design_decision_supported: Measured well-pair changes and modeled surface changes are distinct products; changes in head are not by themselves storage or budget estimates.

citation: Heath RC and USGS Circular 1217.
specific_design_decision_supported: Hydrogeologic units and boundaries require independent evidence; splitting interpolation prevents cross-region influence but does not impose a numerical flow boundary condition.

citation: USGS Circular 1217 Box A and Basic Ground-Water Hydrology.
specific_design_decision_supported: A plan-view head surface sampled along a line is a visualization; wells retain their screened interval and offset and the result is not a three-dimensional flow model.

citation: Open Geospatial Consortium Styled Layer Descriptor specification.
specific_design_decision_supported: SLD output is standards-based XML; styling encodes line pattern as well as color and must not contain private paths.
